utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Good morning, everybody. The case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the appearances. For the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning. Nicholas Koumjian, with Ruth Karper, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you prepared to start immediately with the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise because yesterday, I prepared myself for the cross-examination, but Dr. Stakic instructed me that we are not going to cross-examine this witness. And I apologise once again for leaving this witness overnight. But we just established this this morning, talking about these signature issues. I visited my client this morning here prior to this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I believe you shouldn't apologise. We appreciate the outcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic expressed this because of the suffering of this witness and his pretty bad mental state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this understanding. But I think it seems to be necessary to excuse formally the witness. May the witness please be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning. Please be seated immediately. Mr. Karagic, this morning, we learned that the accused waived his right to have a cross-examination by Defence counsel. Therefore, there will be no additional questions put to you by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I have a desire to add something, regardless of what he thinks, with your permission of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of course, it's your right. And hereby I formally ask you, do you have to add anything to what you stated yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there are always details that can be added, though I don't know how important they are for you. However, there is something that I think is important, at least it is to me. Although you probably know everything already, because you have all my previous statements. On the other hand, if it's not necessary for me to add anything or to repeat things, maybe then that would be it. But of course, if you wish me to say something more, I'll be happy to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You must know, only this what we have heard in the courtroom, only this counts, not former written reports or statements which, indeed, they are available for us. But when you feel that it's necessary for you and you want to tell us something in addition to what you told us yesterday, probably rethinking after the hearing of yesterday, please feel free to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It concerns the very beginning of my story. I don't remember having told you anything about the cleansing itself, at least I'm not sure. And, also, the ultimatum that was issued by them, which was followed by the attack on Hambarine and this attack on the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Probably for the clarity of the proceedings, I think it's more appropriate that we regard this what follows now as continuation of the examination-in-chief because it seems to be in addition to that. May I ask, Mr. Koumjian, please take over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps the ELMO could be lowered, the arm. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Karagic, yesterday you briefly talked about the shelling of Hambarine, which we understood the first time was at the end of May, 1992. And you also then talked in more detail about events regarding the cleansing of your village which, am I correct, that that happened in July of 1992? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just a second. Let me think. It's difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We understand that. If there are any details, dates --

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, it has been ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That's very understandable. But prior to the attack on Hambarine, did you hear anything about an ultimatum that was issued?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When this incident took place at the checkpoint in Hambarine --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to be clear, you were not present at the checkpoint in Hambarine when the incident took place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. I wasn't, but some people ran up to the checkpoint after fire had been opened on them. Later, people told us about it and we learned about what had happened. The ultimatum was issued over the radio on that night, and there were several shells that were fired during that night. And the ultimatum expired by 12.00. Aziz Aliskovic, Sikiric, whose name I don't know but who was from Hambarine, were there at the checkpoint and the ultimatum concerned them. They were supposed to be handed over. I cannot remember all of the details but I remember that the ultimatum was also about the weapons which were supposed to be surrendered. So the next day, at about 12.00, and they were on time, the shelling started from all sides: from the Urije neighbourhood, which is in Prijedor, from the Topic hill, from Karana. I'm not sure about Lisejka but I heard that it was also from there. But the locations that I mentioned were something that I could see myself because, when the shelling started, I ran to the Rizvanovici checkpoint, which was located there in the direction of Tukovi. Because it was the first time that I witnessed something like that. And every time I heard the detonation, I would throw myself onto the ground. But I could see everything. I could see shells falling down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did anyone fire at the checkpoint in Rizvanovici?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sometime later, a cleansing took place in Rizvanovici, is that correct, what you call a "cleansing"? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was an ethnic cleansing. But it took place later on, and it went on in July as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You've used that word "cleansing," and "ethnic cleansing" you just used a couple times. Can you tell us what you mean when you say a cleansing took place?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when this word was used, I was not familiar with it. But later, everybody kept referring to the event as "the cleansing." So did I. I don't know how else to call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: What would happen in a cleansing? What was the pattern that you saw?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The night before the cleansing, shells were fired on the Rizvanovici village. Some hit the wooded area on the other side of the Rizvanovici field, but not far from the houses. Some shells landed in the farms and the yards. I could see that myself. So the next day, the next morning, very early that morning, I was at the location called Sljunkara. Then we went to -- first, we were actually in the area called Luka, and then we went to Sljunkara or to the quarry. There were two neighbours with me: One was from Hambarine and one was my next-door neighbour, actually, a person from my village. There was another young man by the name of Djoni. We were all hungry. This neighbour of mine wanted me to go home and get some food, but I didn't want to. He and his cousin went home before me, so me and this young man called Johnny were the first ones to have seen the beginning of this cleansing, when they started shooting and throwing hand grenades. We ran away immediately. He ran in a different direction. I went in the direction of Solsa [phoen]. They were shouting after me, telling me not to run. But I continued, of course, and finally arrived in an area which is in the vicinity of my house, where a number of people had gathered. From that vantage point, we were able to see the whole area of Prijedor and we could see soldiers taking up positions around the village. Of course, I couldn't see everything, but I could tell that there were quite a few of them. I asked the people around me, my neighbours, "What are we going to do? Shall we run? Shall we flee?" Because we didn't have anything to defend ourselves with. And they said: "Well, we're not guilty of anything. They cannot possibly harm us in any way." They simply didn't believe that that would happen. But anyway, with two other neighbours, I escaped to the creek and we took shelter in a ditch where there was still some water running. It seems strange now, but they were already there, some 3 or 4 metres above the ditch, and we were down below in the ditch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: When you talk about "they were there," and you talked about the people throwing hand grenades and shooting in your village, and "they took up positions around the village," you said, are you referring, am I correct, that all these times you're referring to soldiers of the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those whom I was able to see were wearing military olive-grey uniforms. I couldn't see all of them, but before I went into hiding, I managed to see distinctly three of them, although there were many more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you see any individuals with police or reserve police uniforms during the cleansing of your village?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I couldn't see anything because I was hidden in the stream. I could just hear the shooting coming from all sides, and people screaming, of course. But actually, that happened later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You said earlier that they were shooting and throwing hand grenades. What were they shooting and throwing hand grenades at, could you see?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the cleansing began, they threw hand grenades. But the night before, they fired shells on the village. I don't remember that they shelled the village during the cleansing, because that would have endangered themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: When they were throwing hand grenades, did you see what the targets were, where the hand grenades exploded?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hand grenades?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the hand grenades.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't see that. They were probably throwing those on the houses as they were passing through the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And you said -- did you later see damage to the houses?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN KARAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about this stream. We stayed there until nightfall. Before that, we didn't dare go close to the houses. The shooting lasted the entire day. They had a lot of work to do. But they didn't meet any resistance. When I came home, I found my mother there. These two other guys went home to get some food as well. While I was at home -- I mean, I didn't actually enter the house. My mother gave me some food through the window. A man came from the village of Duratovici, but we called the area Sabari [phoen], and he told me what happened in their village because their village was the first one that was targeted. So there were not many survivors in their village. My uncle was killed there, my father's brother, who was quite old. He was killed there. And this other uncle, the younger one, he was also killed behind the Munib Karagic's house. His wife told us about that. And this Ferid person, I don't know whether I have mentioned his surname -- I shouldn't have mentioned it, if I did. It would not be in his interest. Anyway, Ferid, it was in front of his shop. He owned a shop, you see, that this happened. What I'm trying to say is that there were 20 or 30 dead bodies outside his shop of the people who had been killed. Across the street from his shop, there were also dead bodies in about the same number. I mean, all of this is something that I did not personally eyewitness. These are the stories that I heard later on. I also heard that they made a young man jump from a two or three metre height into a brook which was only several centimetres deep. I think he was killed as a result of that. I believe that they called him Pekar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karagic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this additional information you gave us this morning. I have to ask formally the Defence, any questions? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I see there are no additional questions. Judge Fassi Fihri, no questions. Judge Vassylenko, no questions. Then we all have to thank you for this, I believe for you, very difficult hearing providing us with these numerous informations. And you can be quite sure that the informations will be in good hand, and we all wish you that everything is possible and will be provided for you to overcome all that what you experienced in the future. Thank you for being here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for having listened to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have to continue with our proceedings. There are now... First of all, when discussing the results of previous hearings, the Bench came to the conclusion that it would be helpful to have the handwritten notes of Mr. McLeod admitted into evidence. Is the OTP prepared to tender this entire binder of the handwritten notes starting with the registration number 02052611 until 02052713?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I believe that would be no problem. They are not actually physically present at the moment. We can get those in a few minutes or at the break. Of course, it would be a copy of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I then no doubt have to come back to this later on. Then it seems to be necessary to read out, and I emphasise with a view to the booth, first of all, a very limited number of documents because we can't discuss these documents without knowing about the contents during the then-following Status Conference. And therefore, let us, please, turn to the documents in list 2 and 3. And I would invite the Prosecutor to inform us which documents allegedly be signed by Dr. Stakic. They would add in the framework of the discussion of our Status Conference. Therefore, please be prepared immediately after the break to have these documents present and, hopefully, also the binder on the originals, that we know what we are discussing in detail, having the documents before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The originals of most of these documents are being copied now, so we don't physically have the originals today because the Trial Chamber asked for coloured copies. So that's where they are at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: They are not in the premises?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think they are copied outside the premises. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we have to proceed on the basis of the documents we have before us. But please, as we, the Judges, don't know what you provided for the Defence, be prepared that we have the other documents where it's contested that the documents are signed by Dr. Stakic, that they form part of the reading-out exercise now or immediately after the break. We should start -- please correct me if I'm wrong. The last time we read out Document 78, the 17th of June. And then the next one would be Document S79. What's the best arrangement that the booth has the document available? I think it would indeed facilitate, if the French booth doesn't object fundamentally, to read it out in English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay, Exhibit S79.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the document please be placed on the ELMO, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If it helps, 65 ter 248. "Handwritten, circulation 1D/? Dusan Jankovic, 1D Jankovic. Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Autonomous Region of Krajina, Municipality of Prijedor. Number: 02/111/215/92. Date: 17th of June, 1992. "Pursuant to Articles 3 and 7 on the decision of the organisation and work of the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Prijedor, the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Prijedor at its session on 17 June, 1992, and in connection with the report on the security situation in the area of the municipality, adopted the following order: "1. The Prijedor public security station and the Prijedor regional command are ordered to form a joint intervention platoon to be made up of 20 members from each, with a basic task of preventing looting and other criminal activities in the area of the municipality and the movement of all unregistered vehicles and vehicles driven by members of the army and police without regularly approved travel authorisation. "2. The members of the platoon from the previous item shall be chosen from among the existing members of the army and police. "3. The Crisis Staff shall give its consent to the members proposed for the platoon by the regional command and the public security station. "4. The regional command and the public security station are obliged to submit a written report on the activities and the work results of the intervention platoon to the municipal Crisis Staff within seven days. "5. This order comes into effect on the date of its adoption. "Sent to: Public security station. Regional command Prijedor. Files. "President of the Crisis Staff, Dr. Milomir Stakic." A signature, and a stamp of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Probably when we go to the B/C/S document within the stamp, there seems to be a "Za" to be read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry. It appears to me that there is a "Za," and it may even be Spiro Marmat's signature - I'm not sure about that - who was the secretary for the Crisis Staff. But I want to make it clear that we believe the accused is absolutely responsible for this just as I sign --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That's another question. Just that we have categories, and here I think the parties can agree that the signature is not the signature of Dr. Stakic. The responsibility for this is a totally different question. Right? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We agree, Your Honour, that actually most of the signatures are not the signature of Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. May we then turn to Document 80, please, which was 253.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Autonomous Region of Krajina, Prijedor Municipality, Crisis Staff. Number: 02-111-258/92. Date: 23rd of June, 1992. "Pursuant to Article 7 of the decision on the organisation and work of the Prijedor Municipality Crisis Staff, the following conclusion was adopted by the Prijedor Municipality Crisis Staff at the session held on 23rd June, 1992. "Conclusion: "1. Funds from the Prijedor SO Municipal Assembly budget in the amount of 55.727.880 dinars have been approved for public services in the Prijedor Municipality as follows: "1.1 To beneficiaries of the education sector in the amount of 54.550.250 dinars of which: "1.11 For elementary education, 36.378.063 dinars. "1.12 For secondary streamed education, 18.157.187 dinars. "1.2 To users of the cultural centre, Kozara museum, the amateur theatre, the national library, and the municipal KPZ cultural and educational association, in the amount of 1.222.640 dinars. "2. Funds for the services in question will be transferred directly from the budget account to the transfer account of the beneficiaries of the public services according to criteria determined by the Prijedor SO Crisis Staff, and will be used only to pay employees' salaries. "3. The municipal secretary of the economy and public services will be responsible for carrying out this conclusion. "2.1 Secretary of the economy and public services. "2.2 SDK. "3. Records. "4. Archives."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The following document will be the former 65 ter 257, which is now S81.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't know it Your Honour wants to ask me the same question, but I do believe I see a "Za" on the seal on this document also, just before the Presidency is written in the -- say the north-east corner of the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had the chance to see the best original the Prosecution has and, at any rate, at the beginning, we got the documents S77, S79, and S80. We found that all the signatures are different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But we have to do it document by document, and here I think we can agree that one can see a "Za," and apparently the signature is totally different from the one which was not contested, as I think it was three times, the signature of Dr. Stakic. So once again, this is in the category whether or not we have the responsibility of Dr. Stakic even though he hasn't signed the document. But here I think the parties agree that this is not the signature of Dr. Stakic. May we now turn to Document 80.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "Handwritten, Simo Markovic. Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Handwritten, 49. Krajina Autonomous Region. Handwritten, interrogation mark 50. Prijedor Municipality Crisis Staff. Number: 02-111-237/92. Date: 23rd June, 1992. "Pursuant to articles 3 and 7 of the decision on the organisation and work of the Prijedor Municipality Crisis Staff, the Prijedor Municipality Crisis Staff at a session held on 23rd June, 1992, took the following decision: "One, it is forbidden to use funds from the accounts of economic enterprises and independent shops whose owners were killed, have moved away, or were arrested for armed insurrection. "Two, approval is hereby given to the municipal secretariat for the economy to temporarily use the funds in the giro accounts of the /people/ referred to in the preceding paragraph in the form of a loan. "Three, the Prijedor SDK public auditing service and the municipal secretariat of the economy shall see to the implementation of this decision. "Four, this decision comes into effect on the day it is adopted. "Delivered to: 1, Prijedor SDK; 2, municipal secretariat for the economy; 3, files. "Handwritten for president of the Crisis Staff, Milomir Stakic." A signature and stamped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Signature? Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see that number 80 is mentioned. Is it number 80 or 81?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We are discussing 81, yes. Right. 81. The former 257, that there is no doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As I mentioned, we were given 23 documents, and on those 23 documents, we found six different signatures. And this signature falls into category six. So this is not the signature of Dr. Stakic as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Prosecution, observations?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't have any observation other than to say that it appears to be different than, for example, the signature on the next document, which is one we definitely contend is the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: At least to the negative, what is not the signature. May we then turn to the former 267, which is now 82. And here, we have a set of documents evidently underlying in B/C/S in A-4 format. Then a printed version of this in the newspaper Glas from 26 June, 1992, and then this English interpretation. Would you please be so kind and read out the English interpretation, 82A.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document was subdivided as 82. I read both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "Handwritten, 26 June, 1992. Announcement on the cancellation of job openings. "Pursuant to Articles 3 and 7 on the Decision of the Organisation and Work of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality, at a session held on 6 June, 1992, the Prijedor Municipality Crisis Staff decided to cancel the opening for headmasters of the elementary schools in Prijedor Municipality announced in Glas on 25 May, 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then it continues on the next page because there are two parts of a newspaper.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "30th of June, 1992, marks an end to 40 days of pain and grief following the death of our dear uncle." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What is the nexus between these two documents, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm not sure I even have that last translation. If I'm -- I'm not sure about the last item. My understanding was that the newspaper article discussed the decision that is in the -- that is the next page that's signed by -- under the signature of Dr. Stakic or under his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But through the document, I wondered if there is really a nexus between this additional outclip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You're talking about the very small clip?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. You can see the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I see. I do now see it. I don't see any, other than the fact that it is the following page on the ERN. So it could be withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we can forget about this additional clip. And then we have to return to the underlying decision, if this could be --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Someone -- Ms. Karper had a suggestion which is probably correct as an explanation: This probably was the back of the piece of paper; both the front and back of the newspaper article were photocopied. So the back is unrelated but it's on the original piece of paper which has the article in the front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we now turn to the decision itself, as we have it in the form of a decision, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Autonomous Region of Krajina, Prijedor Municipality Crisis Staff. Number: 02-111-147/92. Date: 6 June, 1992. "Pursuant to Article 7 of the Decision and Organisation of Work of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality, the Prijedor Municipality Crisis Staff, at a session held on 6 June, 1992, issued the following decision with regard to the job opening announcement for elementary schools in the municipality of Prijedor. DECISION "1. The job opening announcement for headmasters of elementary schools has been cancelled. "The mandate of the present headmasters of present elementary schools has been extended until further notice. "2. This decision shall enter into force on the day it is issued. "CC, 1, Secretariat for Economic Affairs; 2, headmasters of elementary schools; 3, files. "Chairman of the Crisis Staff, signed and stamped, Dr. Milomir Stakic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let us now turn to this signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the signature of the accused. That's our contention. We have no doubt about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to comment. This part of the newspapers, something has been added. The date is handwritten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I just want to have this on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Handwritten over "Glas."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Handwritten and underlined. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Regarding the signature, it falls into category 2 and is the same as S77, but different from others read today. So it is not the signature of Dr. Stakic.

utterances.text: "Official Gazette of Prijedor Municipality. Thursday, 25 June, 1992. Issue 2/92. "18. "At its session of 20 May, 1992, Prijedor Municipal Assembly, pursuant to Article 110 of the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Official Gazette of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, issue number 3/92 adopted the following: "Decision on the organisation and work of Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff. "Article 1: Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff is hereby established and its organisation and sphere of action set out. "Article 2: Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff has been established to coordinate the functions of the authorities, the defence of the municipal territory, the protection of safety of people and property, the establishment of government, and the organisation of all other fields of life and work. As coordinator, the Crisis Staff shall create conditions enabling the Municipal Executive Committee to discharge its legal executive functions, manage the economy, and other areas of life. "Article 3: Should the Municipal Assembly be unable to sit in session, Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff shall decide on matters falling within the province of the assembly jurisdiction. "As soon as it is possible to convene a session of the assembly, it shall be the duty of the Crisis Staff to submit for endorsement all decisions which it has adopted and which would normally fall within the province of the assembly. "Article 4: Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff shall have a president, a vice-president, and nine members. "The President of the Municipal Assembly shall serve ex officio as the president of the Crisis Staff, and the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly as the vice-president of the Crisis Staff. "The following shall serve as members of the Crisis Staff: The President of the Municipality Executive Committee, Commander of the Municipal Territorial Defence Staff, Commander of the Municipal People's Defence Staff, Chief of the Public Security Station, Secretary of Municipal Secretariat for Trade, Industry, and Public Services, Secretary of the Municipal Secretariat for Town Planning, Housing, Utilities, and Legal Property Affairs, the Health and Social Security Officer at Municipal Secretariat for the Economy and Social Affairs, and Information Officer at Municipal Secretariat for the Economy and Social Affairs. "Article 5: In accordance with the assessment of the political and security situation and realistic requirements, the Crisis Staff shall adopt relevant decisions on the organisation and work of the Municipal Assembly, its organs, and other municipal organs and local communes. "Article 6: In discharging its functions in the area of defence, the Crisis Staff shall, in particular, coordinate the work and activities of all components of all people's defence, consider issues of mobilisation, development and reinforcement of the armed forces and other organisations and foster their cooperation with other responsible municipal organs; on special request of the Commander of the Municipal Territorial Defence staff, deal with issues of supply requirements and funding sources for the TO; keep abreast of all aspects of the situation in the municipality essential for the waging of armed combat and take appropriate measures; monitor the implementation of the recruitment plan and, where necessary, take measures for successful implementation thereof. "Article 7: In exercising its functions from the fields of the economy and social affairs, the Crisis Staff shall in particular: Adopt decisions relevant to the organisation and functioning of the economy in the public, private, and mixed ownership sectors, the organisation and functioning of social affairs, the organisation and management of finance sector, and the care of refugees and the destitute; where necessary, decide on the introduction of food and strategically important supply rationing; monitor the implementation of the aforementioned decisions by considering municipal executive committee reports and issue specific orders to eliminate eventualities which might complicate or preclude their implementation. "Article 8: In discharging its functions in civil defence and the monitoring and reporting service /as printed/ the Crisis Staff shall in particular, through Municipal Civil Defence Staff and other agencies, take measures to achieve the highest possible degree of civil defence readiness for the accomplishment of its tasks and through Municipal People's Defence Secretariat take measures and action for the successful functioning of the communications centre and the monitoring and reporting service. "Article 9: The Crisis Staff shall at all times cooperate with the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, civil defence, and public security, through the senior officers or organs of these institutions. The Crisis Staff shall cooperate with all other businesses and public organisations in the municipality through the municipal executive committee. "Article 10: The Crisis Staff shall create conditions for the work of the international peace and humanitarian organisations and facilitate unhindered passage of convoys carrying humanitarian aid through the territory of the municipality. "Article 11: The provisions of the constitution, the law and decisions adopted by the Assembly, the Presidency, and the government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the responsible organs of the Autonomous Region of the Banja Luka Krajina have been and shall remain the foundation for the work of Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff. "Article 12: The Crisis Staff shall gather all relevant information on the situation on the ground, report and consult with the competent organs of the Autonomous Region of the Banja Luka Krajina and with those of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina whenever required or possible. "Article 13: This decision shall enter into force on the day it is adopted. "Article 14: This decision shall remain in force as long as a need exists for the work of the Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff. Prijedor Municipal Assembly may adopt a decision revoking this decision. "Article 15: This decision shall be published in the Official Gazette of Prijedor Municipality. "No. 01-023-24/92. Prijedor. Date: 20 May 1992. "Dr. Milomir Stakic, President, Municipal Assembly."

utterances.text: I don't have a date, but I can determine. In a moment, I can give you where this document was recovered. This was in the 1997 search of the SDS offices in Prijedor, this document was recovered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But the problem remains open, that we have a supplement to the minutes and apparently we don't know which minutes from what date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That's correct. But what I will try to do is to check the ERN range before that to see if there was -- this was attached or recovered with another document. But we -- at least this sheet is not dated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Comments from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As my learned friend from the opposite stated, that this is one of the different kinds of a signature of Dr. Stakic. So it's obvious that it's not the same as other signatures. And I discussed this document before with Dr. Stakic. He does not remember that he written or signed anything of this nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. This document, in order to remain in the order of the list, will then be admitted into evidence as S179A and B. And the document 444, we have to come back now, unfortunately, not having the English translation at hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It will be here shortly. Perhaps I could take advantage of the delay of the moment to indicate that we have copies, as the Court requested, of the Official Gazette, of the entire gazette number 2. And we also have copies of gazette number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The question was, do you have the original of the gazette that we may have a look on this document, or do you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You just want to see the actual gazette that we recovered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The actual gazette, yes. That was our intention. But we are grateful to receive by the usher now this entire document. The Defence has the entire Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can't check it right now, Your Honour, but if possible, we would like to have a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, give one copy to the Defence first. Is it the understanding that this document is tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Two separate documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Two separate. Yes. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Just a couple problems to bring to the Court's attention before you make a decision. I'm not sure that the entire number 2 has been translated. I was informed that that may not be completely translated. And not all of those decisions we believe are necessarily relevant, and I know that there's an issue of translation of documents. Just for the Court's information, it's a lengthy document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I haven't seen it before. It may provide an impression in its entirety, when we have the document before us in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to stall for more time, I'll just make a brief comment. I think that the documents have arrived. But just referring to the -- briefly mentioned, counsel raised something that happened in the Brdjanin/Talic case, a comment by Ms. Korner. I looked at the context in which that was stated, and would be happy to provide transcripts to anyone who is interested. The context was she was talking about AID statements where there was an issue about whether -- that's the Bosniak service, federation service. There was an issue about whether or not the witnesses or witness had signed a statement that was not offered by the OTP into evidence. And I believe hat if you look at the entire context of her remarks, she is not in any way indicating that we intend to offer into evidence documents that we believe are false. That clearly was not the intention of her remarks. And it's not our belief that any of the documents that we're offering into evidence are falsified in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this comment. The Official Gazette of Prijedor Municipality of 25 June, 1992, is admitted into evidence as S180A, the English translation; and 180B, the copy of the original. And we hope to get -- at least to see once here in the courtroom the original Official Gazette. And then the Official Gazette from the 31st of August, 1992, is admitted into evidence under number S181A, English; and S181B in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And Your Honour, the translations, one is a translation and one is a draft translation, have arrived, and they can be distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Translation for Document 444?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I believe the longer document is 444 and the shorter one would be S177A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could we then, please, start, and read out Document S177A.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Autonomous Region of Krajina, Municipality of Prijedor, Crisis Staff. Number: 02-111-23-I/92. "Date: 6 July 1992. "The decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Banja Luka number 03-351/92 dated 22nd, June, 1992 has been delivered to the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor Municipality. The decision is being forwarded to you for the purpose of its implementation. "President of the Crisis Staff, Dr. Milomir Stakic /signed and stamped/."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And then, please, the draft translation of the former 65 ter Document 444, which is now S178A.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "Republika Srpska, Prijedor Municipal Assembly, Defence Council. "Confidential number: 01-498/96. "Date: 20 March 1996. "Extract from the minutes of an extraordinary session of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly Defence Council held at 1500 hours on 20 March, 1996, in the small hall of Prijedor Municipal Assembly. "The session was attended by Dr. Milomir Stakic, President of the Municipal Assembly; Dr. Aleksandar Bereta, President of the Municipal Board of the Serbian Democratic Party; Vukan Tubin, Chairman of the Municipal Executive Committee; Colonel Pero Colic, Assistant Commander of the Operation Group 10; Lieutenant-Colonel Radovan Smitran, Commander of the 43rd Prijedor Motorised Brigade; Major Radovan Ilc, Commander of the 5th Kozara Brigade; Slavko Budimir, Chief of the Ministry of Defence Section; Mile Medjed, Deputy Chief of the State Security Department Centre; and Svetozar Petrovic, Secretary of the Municipal Assembly. "The session was chaired by the President, Milomir Stakic. "The following agenda was established for the session: "1: Current issues regarding the resolution of the problems of military installations and the materiel situation of members of the 43rd Motorised Brigade, Prijedor Motorised Brigade and the 5th Kozara Brigade. AD-1. The following took part in the discussion: Lieutenant-Colonel Radovan Smitran, Colonel Pero Colic, Major Radovan Ilic, Vukan Tubin, Dr. Aleksandar Bereta, and Dr. Milomir Stakic. "The following issues were singled out in particular: The necessity of securing land and buildings for two barracks in Prijedor Municipality [for the 43rd Prijedor Motorised Brigade and the 5th Kozara Brigade], including a building for an army centre; the necessity of providing money to pay the soldiers and Reserve Office Corps of the 43rd Prijedor Motorised Brigade and 5th Kozara Brigade; the priority resolution of accommodation issues for refugee members of the army; the priority return of mobilised vehicles for commerce and public services; the necessity for representatives of the army to establish as soon as their own capabilities and to state as specifically as possible their requirements to be financed or provided by the municipality. "Following the discussion, during which several other issues were raised, the following were adopted: "Conclusions: "1: In future, material to be considered at a Defence Council session shall be sent in good time. "2: Representatives of the army must sent in writing all requests regarding army requirements [finances, land, buildings, flats, [houses, building and other types of material and equipment, et cetera] to the Prijedor Municipality Executive Committee. Requests must be specific and itemised. "3: Representatives of the army must send requests for the priority resolution of accommodation issues for the Officer Corps for the Executive Committee. "Similarly, they must state their requirements for resolving the accommodation issues of refugee members of the army. "4: Refugee members of the army who are demobilised shall be sent immediately to the Ministry Department for Refugees and Displaced Persons in order to resolve their accommodation issues. "5: Mobilised vehicles shall be returned to Commerce and Public Services as a matter of urgency through the Ministry of Defence Department. "6: Representatives of the army shall be recommended to retain as much as possible vehicles classified as war booty, particularly those that are special purpose. They should be stored and lent for temporary use by health care organisations and enterprises in the municipality according to special procedure. "7: Bearing in mind the serious materiel situation in the municipality, the municipality could temporarily provide pay for a maximum of 1.000 to 1.200 members of the army. "8: Representatives of the army are recommended to plan work units of demobilised refugee members of the army to be engaged in clearing up damaged residential buildings over a certain period. "9: The proposal for the relevant municipal organs, in agreement with the leadership of the SDS/Serbian Democratic Party /municipal board/, to prepare an appropriate informative text giving the most important instructions and directions on how and the manner in which citizens, and particularly refugees, should resolve their accommodation, subsistence, and other issues shall be supported. This text will be broadcast several times by Radio Prijedor. "10: The Chief of the Ministry of Defence Department and Secretary of the Municipal Assembly shall be responsible for preparing a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. draft normative/statute/ for the Municipal Assembly Defence Council. "These conclusions completed the agenda for the session. "Sent to: 1: Council members; 2: Files. "President, Dr. Milomir Stakic /signed and stamped/"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this. May I first hear the comments of the OTP to this document from apparently 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the Court's information, the document was collected in this binder because we were identifying all possible exhibits with the accused's signature, and we do believe this has his signature again. It appears to be "S. Milomir."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Comments by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We saw that the document is outside of the scope of the indictment, but we are glad that the Prosecution provided these documents. We are not telling that the Prosecution has to do anything with this, but it's obvious that the document is tampered. These kind of extracts are never signed. So obviously, something has been done with the document afterwards. So we have the same objections, and previously on top of the objection that it's outside of the scope of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In this context, first of all, it may be that the documents save us -- serves for clarification on the issue of signatures or, as it is submitted by the Defence, for the verification of signatures. So this concludes this round of discussion of signatures or not signatures. We have now to find a way to categorise this. And I tried, and I invite the parties to add some new categories, if possible, that we know what we are discussing. I believe there is one category where the signature of Dr. Stakic is accepted. This is true for Documents S96, S101 and S105. Then we have a second category where you can find a signature, very neutral, "Stakic," as for example on the document just read out. Or is it the position of the OTP that this is more in the direction of "Milomir"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I believe that that's an "S. Milomir."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. But nevertheless, the second category would be where we can find something like "Stakic." Then we have a third category where one can find something like "Milomir" in Cyrillic; a fourth category where one can find something like "Milomir" in Latin. We have a fifth category, other signatures on documents where one can read typed, "Dr. Milomir Stakic," but evidently other persons signing, sometimes with the addition of the two -- of the word "Za," "for," or on behalf of. And then we have a sixth category where there is no signature at all but only we can find typed, "Dr. Milomir Stakic." And finally, seventh category, that we can find a document under which we have Dr. Milomir Stakic" printed in the Official Gazette. The question is now how to proceed? As regards the categories 2, 3, 4, probably including 5, the Bench believes, as already indicated before, that it's necessary to have here the appointment of a handwriting expert; and in addition, the appointment of a typewriter expert to determine whether the documents emanate from the same machine, be it a typewriting machine, be it a printer connected with a PC. Therefore, may I ask, first of all, the party who has the burden of proof, what is the intention how to proceed from their point of view, before we come to ruling under Rule 98?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: First, we acknowledge that the Trial Chamber under Rule 98 has the right to seek any evidence that would be beneficial to you. We believe that we will prove or have proved beyond a reasonable doubt the authenticity that these are documents authorised by the accused. And that is the key issue. Regarding the signatures, I think the actual signed documents, I would put them in three broad categories: one, signatures that we don't believe are necessarily from the accused, they have a "Za," for example; and two, signatures from Stakic in Cyrillic. And Your Honour indicated that there was "Milomir" in Cyrillic and Latin, and I'm no expert in Cyrillic handwriting especially, but just my brief understanding was that those signatures, which look very similar to me, were in Latin, "S. Milomir." But obviously the "S" would look very different in Cyrillic or in Latin. Those seem to be the signatures that are most in dispute as far as whether or not they are or are not the accused, the "S. Milomir" signatures which are on several key documents. We believe that the evidence shows that that is the accused's signature. That's the only reasonable inference. There has been no evidence in Court to the contrary. And the reason I say that is, one, these documents appear several times on several documents seized not from Bihac or from Sarajevo or from someone giving it to us, but seized from places like public security station in Prijedor, the SDS offices in Prijedor. Secondly, many of these documents are published, already published in a gazette. It would make absolutely no sense, it would not be reasonable to believe that someone has forged the accused's signature, published it in a gazette without his authorisation. Finally, several of the documents that have been presented today, I think it would be completely unreasonable to believe that they do not contain the signature of the accused. One of them would be that very last document in the notebook, where it indicated that Dr. Stakic objected to the procedure regarding personnel changes and it indicated the authenticity of this statement is certified. For Your Honours' information, I have been trying to -- you asked about the date, and I did check. We did have someone check. The ERN range just before that contains - in other words, the numbers just before that - contains documents from an SDS meeting, minutes of an SDS meeting in November 1991. I cannot say for sure that they were attached or even found in the same drawer but it makes sense to me that because of the order and when we get the original, perhaps we'll see the situation. The other two documents were the first two documents in the binder, the first one being former 65 ter number 10, which indicated that it's from, again, very early, January 1991, and has the "S. Milomir." And even much more importantly, the second document, dated the 14th of November, 1991, which is a document regarding signatures for people that go to a bank. These are the authorised signatures of people who can write cheques, basically, can disburse funds on this signature from the bank. You don't have -- I could have someone else, Ms. Karper or someone, sign my name for me for a document with my authorisation, but I don't ask Ms. Karper or someone else to go and put her signature on my bank account. It doesn't make sense that the bank account signature is not that of the person who is going to have the authority to disburse funds. Recording Your Honours' request for a handwriting sample, we don't oppose that at all. But we raise a couple of issues. I don't propose to do it myself first because I have very -- in my experience -- I'm not an expert in graphology, but in my experience, a single signature "S. Milomir" will not be sufficient for an expert to make a positive identification that this was written by an individual. In my experience, it requires more writing. But secondly, a bigger problem, we don't have anything to compare it with unless the accused -- and we asked before, and they indicated they did not want to provide it, we don't have a known sample to compare that signature to, unless Your Honours want to ask the expert to compare, for example, that signature on the bank account with other signatures, but the accused has denied that signature also. So I don't think it would get us that far. Again, we have no objection to checking the machine, the typewriting, but I'm not sure how far that will get us. If it indicates one machine or two, the accused will still say that was forged on one machine or forged on two machines. If it's written on various machines, that's very likely that if decisions are -- I don't know how many machines were available to the SDS or to the accused or to the people working with him. I'm not sure how far it will get us. We don't oppose that. But those are the reasons I want to make it clear why we believe it would not be particularly helpful in the case and we believe that, in the entire context of how these documents were found and what they state, the only reasonable inference is these are authentic documents signed and/or authorised by the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May we now hear the comments by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. First of all, we would like that the record reflects that we had a chance to see some documents that are originals allegedly, and the document S106 is actually -- actually, the document which was shown to us has a signature in photocopy and has original stamp on top of that photocopied signature. I believe that we didn't have a chance to see the document which bears the ERN number 00633806 on which we also could find photocopied signature stamped with the original stamp; and the same for the document with the ERN number 00633814. So, first of all, we would like that Your Honours check whether these statements are correct and to confirm, on the record, the form of these documents. Regarding Your Honour's proposition to have an expertise by a handwriting expert, in general, we don't oppose the proposal. But knowing the practice of this Tribunal, we are not ready to waive the right of our client to remain silent, which includes his right not to give a sample of his handwriting. So if you need more clarifications, I can provide it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for the commentaries. I think it's ripe now for a decision now we have the factual basis. Just briefly, we have before us still a motion under Rule 95. Will there be an updated version of this motion prepared by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As you ordered, by Monday, it will be submitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It will be submitted by Monday, and then only later we will receive the response on the basis of the new motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just make it clear: We're talking about the motion regarding excluding Mr. Sejmenovic's testimony? So I don't have to write the response this weekend. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Therefore, I wanted this clarification --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: One other point just for the Court's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I just add, we are eager to know whether or not the parties could find an agreement as regards Documents D13, D14. These were the documents disclosed under Rule 68 and then tendered by the Defence, and there were some problems. This should be discussed amongst the parties. We expect on Monday the documents in colour copy, and please add the documents requested by the Defence immediately before on the transcript and provide the originals. And then please also provide on Monday the originals of the two Official Gazettes of Prijedor. Then, we should know what about the next witnesses to come for the next two weeks, because we have to take care. There will be a plenary, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. but probably only a plenary limited in time. Maybe there is an additional day possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. My understanding is Mr. Sejmenovic will be back on Monday, and then the next witness is 65 ter number 45. Excuse me. That is Mr. Sejmenovic. The next witness would be 65 ter number 3, followed by 43. So 3, and then 4-3. And I believe that will take us through the Plenary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't want to go once again into details of this, but please understand that we need to be prepared and, therefore, we need the statements, if they are not disclosed until now and if they are not available for the Judges, as it was the case with our last witness. And please do not forget to provide us in due time - we will say two days before - with these documents and the exhibit lists, and as soon as possible, the proofing notes. Of course, we can't go into further detail now, and it should be discussed later about the time schedule of this case immediately after the Court recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If we could just bring up the issue quickly regarding that of the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think we had requested -- we had actually a hole in our schedule. We have a couple days we did not have witnesses for, for the 18th and 19th of July. We were hoping to do the videolink then, but I understand from the registry that that's very difficult or impossible, and a preference would be to do it in September. We don't have a problem, as far as I know, with September but we do have this problem with these two days. And I should also mention that we have a number of witnesses who all want to testify in September. That's a problem, but we expect to finish our case in about the middle of September. But we do have this problem that several of the witnesses, they cannot come in late July to fill that hole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, in this context, do not forget that we, for preparation of the second part of the year, really expect by Monday a list indicating a realistic estimated time for each witness to come and the estimated length of the case of the OTP in future. Until now, we take it that it's undisputed that the end of the Prosecutor's case will be no later than mid of September. Any other issues to be raised today? This is apparently not the case. Then the trial stands adjourned until Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
